Meta Ray-Ban Display shipped 13 days after its 2025-09-17 reveal (~84k units in 2025) with a Sony 12 MP camera and no actuator identified (TechInsights 2026-06-10); Gen 2 was confirmed 'simple fixed focus' on 2025-12-11. Phoenix firmware leaks began 2026-02-25; Seeya started mass production of its 0.91-inch OLEDoS panel in May 2026 with >1m shipped by late August after BOE failed qualification; UDN's 2026-09-13 renders show a 'miniature stereo camera array' and a launch 'pushed to 1H 2027'.

segments.title: Connect 2026 and the autofocus line
segments.text: The own-brand Meta Glasses line launched 2026-06-23. Connect 2026 (2026-09-23) announced Meta VR Glasses at US$1,299.99 for spring 2027: ~100 g, 2412x2288 per eye, 37/26 PPD, four outward cameras for hand tracking and colour passthrough plus four eye-tracking cameras; consumer copy says 'full-color passthrough' while developer pages say 'passthrough with autofocus and depth sensing'. A Reality Labs engineer's LinkedIn post, seen as a forum screenshot of an auto-translation, is paraphrased as saying he led the autofocus work; hands-ons praised the passthrough without describing the focus mechanism. The v207 SDK (2026-09-24) exposes no focus-distance API, the agenda had no camera-hardware session, and no Connect coverage links poLight, TLens or Q Tech. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 shipped the same day with no autofocus claim, and Bosworth said there is 'no new version' of Display hardware (Citi still expects a Display 2 in early 2027) and would not commit to AR glasses in 2027. Announce-to-ship is 159-250 days against 13-34 days for glasses; Varjo's enterprise XR-4 Focal Edition (2023) already offers autofocus passthrough. Connect 2027 falls around September 2027, after the first teardowns.

segments.title: Vision Pro cycle, no actuator evidence
segments.text: Apple's tunable-lens patents (2018-09-21, 2023-05-03, 2023-07-21 with ex-CML CTO Topliss, 2024-03-12 with SMA) are all see-through prescription lenses, not camera autofocus. Vision Pro shipped 242 days after its 2023-06-05 announcement with 12 cameras and no actuator or module supplier identified; the M5 refresh shipped 7 days after announcement (2025-10-22) while production fell to 45,000 units in Q4 2025 from ~390,000 in 2024. The display-accessory glasses were paused Q4 2024 and cancelled January 2025.

segments.title: Register sweep: no Apple TLens trace
segments.text: The round-3 full-text sweep for 'TLens' and 'poLight' across all assignees returned no Apple text that survived the register check: a lens-power metrology grant (US 12,523,846, 2026-01-13) whose variable-focus camera uses liquid-filled or liquid-crystal lenses was left off the map as off-topic, a head-mounted lens-mounting grant matched only on 'lens tabs', and two further Apple list hits were not opened. Apple's tunable-lens patents already on the map (2018-09-21, 2023-05-03, 2023-07-21 with ex-CML CTO Topliss, 2024-03-12 with SMA actuators) remain fluid-filled see-through prescription optics. Across 2024-2026 publications there is no Apple text on a piezo-membrane camera autofocus, no poLight citation and no N50-related camera filing. The absence fits Gurman's two-sensor design with no autofocus reported, but a buyer need not patent a part, and the 18-month publication lag hides anything filed after about April 2025.

segments.title: N50 slippage
segments.text: Gurman's targets moved from end-2026 (2025-05-23, with 'large quantities of prototypes' at end-2025) to reveal-2026/ship-2027 (2025-12-12), mass production December 2026 and launch early 2027 (2026-02-18), late 2027 (2026-05-31) and a WWDC June 2027 unveil with shipments by end-2027 (2026-07-26, reiterated 2026-09-27): about 12 months of slip over 492 days. The design has two camera sensors, capture and computer vision, with no autofocus reported; Kuo expects Q2 2027 mass production and 3-5m+ units in 2027, display glasses in 2029 and the N224 headset on 'life support'. Supplier-side evidence is thin: ex-CML CTO Ben Brown's move and SEMCO's coil deal point to Apple's existing actuator chain, not poLight. Round 2 added only chain-level pointers: Cowell, Vision Pro's external-camera supplier with Apple at 98.1% of revenue, 'hopes to join the Apple AI-glasses project' (Guojin, 2025-11-03); Patrick Llull left Apple for Meta in May 2026 and ex-Apple optics inventors lead Meta's tunable-lens camera-module filing; a forum-posted profile of an Apple Grenoble hardware engineer with PZT tunable-lens research background is rumor-grade.

segments.title: Platform assembly
segments.text: The Magic Leap partnership (May 2024, extended three years on 2025-10-30), Qualcomm's confirmation of joint glasses work (2024-09-05), Android XR's unveiling (2024-12-12), the US$250m HTC acqui-hire (2025-01-23) and Google I/O 2025 prototypes with Gentle Monster, Warby Parker (US$150m commitment) and Kering set the stage; Galaxy XR launched 2025-10-21 and Google said on 2025-12-08 'the first glasses will arrive next year'.

segments.title: 2026 launch, 2027 display
segments.text: Kering's CEO put Gucci glasses at 'probably next year, 2027' (2026-04-16); I/O 2026 (2026-05-19) committed Samsung/Google eyewear to 'this fall', display glasses to 2027 and Xreal Aura to before end-2026; Unpacked London (2026-07-22) formally introduced the eyewear and the FCC cleared SM-O200P/SM-O200J on 2026-10-01 with a Samsung official naming November 2026, 689 days after the Android XR unveil and 166 days after I/O. Nothing from Google addresses camera focus; the 2027 display generation is the window where any new camera module would be designed in.

segments.title: Samsung's T-lens depth-camera family
segments.text: Samsung's register trail is two families, neither naming poLight. US 12,487,379 (priority 2021-07-15, granted 2025-12-02) claims a 7-element lens with a tunable lens between the second and third elements, a polymer plate over sealed liquid-gel pressed by a ring whose actuator 'may include a piezoelectric actuator or a motor'; a Meta application cites it. KR priority 2022-10-31 and its US continuation 19/182,755 (filed 2025-04-18, published 2025-07-31, docketed, no office action) describe a glasses-type device whose second camera's 'focus-variable lens 280 may be a tunable lens (T-lens)' of piezo film, glass membrane, glass panel and transparent polymer, for depth-from-focus. Cadence: priorities in 2021 and 2022, then a US continuation 30 months later, six months before Galaxy XR and 19 months before SM-O200P. The T-lens serves a depth camera that the single-camera FCC device lacks, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the VRARA autofocus rumour; a 2027 examination outcome is a projection.

segments.title: Headset first
segments.text: Joint OS/silicon/hardware design with Google and Qualcomm began in 2023; Project Moohan was named 2024-12-12 and shipped as Galaxy XR on 2025-10-31, ten days after its unveil, at US$1,799.99 with 2x6.5 MP passthrough plus 10 tracking cameras; an aggregator estimates ~40,000 units in 2025. No autofocus was claimed for the passthrough cameras.

segments.title: Glasses: a 19-month slip and an autofocus rumour
segments.text: ETNews reported 'Haean' glasses for 'later this year' on 2025-03-21; three weeks later the target became 2026, confirmed in the Q4-2025 earnings call, at MWC (2026-03-06, camera 'at your eye level'), at I/O (2026-05-19, 'this fall'), at Unpacked (2026-07-22) and by the FCC filing (2026-10-01: single 12 MP camera, AR1 Gen 1, 9 h) with a November 2026 launch, 590 days after the first report. VRARA's 2026-02-09 'early reports' of 12 MP with autofocus (234 days before the FCC filing) remain unconfirmed by Samsung; the leaked spec sheet names a Sony IMX681 at US$379-499. Samsung cites ~200 patent applications and a colour-display 'Haean' for 2027, possibly late 2027.

segments.title: Five Spectacles generations
segments.text: Spectacles shipped in 2016 (vending machines), 2018 (220,000 pairs cumulative by May 2018), 2019, 2021 (first AR display, developer-only) and 2024-09-17 (gen 5, 2 RGB + 2 IR cameras, 226 g, US$99/month for developers). Snap's IR release of 2025-06-10 committed to 'lightweight, immersive Specs in 2026', and Spectacles OS 2.0 (2025-09-15) promised a 'lighter and smaller' sixth generation 'next year'; Guttag called gen 5 'a developer kit, not a consumer product'.

segments.title: Consumer Specs
segments.text: Specs Inc. was formed 2026-01-28 and a multi-year Qualcomm deal signed 2026-04-10; AWE 2026 (2026-06-16, 371 days after the IR commitment) unveiled Specs at US$2,195, 51-degree FOV, 132/136 g, four cameras with no megapixel or focus figure; pre-orders opened 2026-09-16 (92 days later) with a US$200 deposit and shipping 'later this fall' in the US, UK and France, the initial run reportedly capped at ~100,000 units. As of 2026-10-06 specs.com still publishes no camera megapixel or focus specification, so the autofocus question for Specs is open.

segments.title: Display-glasses volume, flat units
segments.text: Xreal sold 137,200 glasses in 2023, 124,900 in 2024 and 133,700 in 2025 (revenue RMB 390m, 395m and 516m; adjusted net loss RMB 250m in 2025) and claimed 51% of worldwide AR share in Q3 2023. One Pro was promised for March 2025 and reached general availability on 2025-07-01, a 122-day slip. The Eye camera accessory shipped in July 2025 as 12 MP, f/2.25, 1.35 g with EIS; its spec page states no focus type, so the 'fixed focus, autofocus not supported' reading carried in the dataset is unsourced. At this volume Xreal is a small buyer of any camera actuator, and it fits poorly the 'very sizable, worldwide known' label poLight gives its leading customers.

segments.title: Aura
segments.text: Project Aura was announced with Google on 2025-05-20, shown at AWE 2025 and CES 2026, and revealed in full at AWE 2026 (2026-06-16, 392 days later): 70-degree FOV, Snapdragon 'Reality Elite' puck, two tracking cameras plus one high-resolution camera of undisclosed focus type, no more than US$1,500, fall 2026 in five countries. A US$100m Series D (Jan 2026), an HKEX filing for up to US$400m (2026-04-01, Luxshare and Alibaba as shareholders) and a patent suit against Viture (2026-01-15) frame the launch; Android Authority's 2026-09-06 hands-on still said 'before the end of 2026'.

segments.title: From AR Lite to Rokid Glasses
segments.text: AR Lite (2024-04-23) was a display product; Rokid Glasses, unveiled 2024-11-14 for Q2 2025, reached Kickstarter only on 2025-08-26 (285 days later) with a 12 MP Sony IMX681 f/2.25 camera, passed US$1m in four days, closed at US$3.6m on 2025-10-10, exceeded US$4m by 2025-11-21 and delivered in November 2025, about five months late. Taiwan crowdfunding set a NT$62m record on 2025-12-12.

segments.title: Volume, fixed focus
segments.text: Ai Glasses Style (38.5 g, 12 MP Sony camera, US$299) was shown at CES on 2026-01-06, available globally 13 days later and past 15,000 units sold by 2026-02-02; Japan crowdfunding took ¥200m in ten days (2026-03-12). A 2026-07-30 review confirmed the camera is fixed focus with a 34 cm minimum distance, so Rokid's volume product carries no actuator at all. Rokid claims 41% of global AR and AI glasses shipments in H1 2026 (its own PR, 2026-09-28).

segments.title: X2 to X3 Pro
segments.text: RayNeo X2 went from CES 2023 to a China debut in November 2023 (~10 months); X2 Lite's 'Q3 2024' promise has no sourced ship date. X3 Pro (CES 2025-01-06) launched in China on 2025-05-27 (141 days) and globally on 2025-12-17 (345 days) with a 12 MP camera of unstated focus type; the V3 camera glasses promised at the same CES with '12 MP IMX681 with HDR and OIS', which would imply an actuator in a 39 g frame, have no ship date 638 days later. Counterpoint gave RayNeo 24% of global AR glasses in Q3 2025.

segments.title: Fast refresh, camera-free turn
segments.text: Air 4 Pro went from CES (2026-01-06) to sale in 19 days; the X3 Pro camera was confirmed as 12 MP IMX681 colour plus a monochrome 6DoF tracking camera on 2026-08-04, focus unstated; the camera-free iO, GT and GT Max were unveiled 2026-08-21 and retailed 14 days later, with X3 Pro cut to US$1,099. RayNeo claims the #1 global AR shipment position for H1 2026. Its newest products drop the camera entirely, the opposite of an autofocus roadmap.

segments.title: Camera-free by design
segments.text: G1 was unveiled 2024-06-26 and G2 (US$599) with the R1 ring followed 504 days later on 2025-11-12 with a 27.5-degree display and no cameras or speakers.

segments.title: Funding without cameras
segments.text: A US$150m pre-Series B at a US$1bn valuation (2026-07-06, Meituan and Tencent) was followed a day later by the CEO stating G3 'will not launch in 2026' and that cameras are not the company's direction; a software overhaul was promised within 1-3 months (2026-07-17). No addressable market for camera autofocus suppliers in 2026-2027.

segments.title: Audio frames
segments.text: Echo Frames generations 1 (2019-09-25, US$179.99), 2 (2020-11-19) and 3 (2023-09-20, from US$269.99) are audio-only with no camera or display, giving Amazon no consumer camera-glasses track record.

segments.title: Driver glasses and the Jayhawk rumour
segments.text: Reuters reported driver glasses 'Amelia' on 2024-11-11; The Information reported consumer 'Jayhawk' (camera plus monocular display) for late 2026/early 2027 on 2025-09-10, with no follow-up in the 391 days since. The delivery glasses with 'integrated cameras' were unveiled 2025-10-22 (763 days after Echo Frames 3), and the 2026-09-21 update counts 275,000 deliveries by 500+ drivers over 18 months, 5,000 more devices in 2026 and 20,000+ by end-2027, an order of magnitude below the rumoured 100,000 initial run. Amazon's AR patents cover UI and fulfilment, not optics or autofocus. The only Amazon-adjacent TLens trace is a forum-posted Foxconn engineer's 'TLens fast-focus camera module driver development' in a 2024 role serving Microsoft, Amazon and Varjo, which fits Varjo's XR-4 rather than Amazon.

segments.title: Quark to Qwen
segments.text: Quark AI Glasses were previewed at WAIC on 2025-07-28 and launched 122 days later (2025-11-27; S1 from 3,799 yuan, G1 from 1,899 yuan, 12 MP, Qualcomm AR1); the renamed Qwen Glasses appeared at MWC 96 days after that (2026-03-03, 12 MP Sony IMX681) with China sales from 2026-03-08 and an international release 'within 2026' that has not yet been dated. Alibaba claimed 53% of China's online smart-glasses sales on 2026-05-08.

segments.title: N1 at 50 MP
segments.text: The N1 series was previewed on 2026-09-10, opened pre-orders 2026-09-22 and goes on sale 2026-10-13 (33 days preview-to-sale) with a 50 MP camera and iris payment, China only, 191 days after the Qwen Glasses drop. The 4-6-month cadence makes a mid-2027 successor likely but unannounced. The only tunable-lens trace in the Alibaba ecosystem is Ant Group's 'Look to Pay' demo glasses with a TLens camera (2026-08-06).

segments.title: Tunable-lens early adopter
segments.text: NEXTLENS was founded in Dietikon in June 2017; Xiaomi's Mitu Children's Learning Watch 4Pro (2020-01-07, 1,299 yuan) shipped an 8 MP 'T-LENS ultra-fast focus' camera, the first commercial poLight TLens product, 4.8 months after poLight's PVT PO of 2019-08-15 and 2.7-2.9 months after the launch-prep POs of 2019-10-11/17, and was named by poLight only in its Q1-2020 report; the Mi MIX Fold (2021-03-30) used a NEXTLENS liquid lens in its telephoto/macro camera.

segments.title: AI Glasses
segments.text: 36Kr reported a Goertek ODM partnership with Lei Jun expecting >300,000 units (2024-11-13); the AI Glasses launched 225 days later (2025-06-26) with a 12 MP Sony IMX681 and Snapdragon AR1 from 1,999 yuan, no autofocus claimed. IT Home's 2026-08-05 report of a completed-but-paused gen 2 slipping to Q4 2026 or 2027 was denied by Xiaomi, 405 days after launch; no supplier signal points at Xiaomi.

segments.title: poLight's named customers: the lead-time ledger
segments.text: XUN's Smartwatch Max Pro (2020-02-10) was the second smartwatch design-win, 5.9 months after its PO; Honeywell's EX30 scan engine with TLens autofocus (2020-10-14) came 7.3 months after the design-in PO; MAXHUB's UC W20 webcam (2021-04-06) launched 5.4 months after its PoC with POs placed after launch. Magic Leap 2's 12.6 MP AF camera was disclosed at SPIE in January 2022 and shipped 2022-09-30; Vuzix Shield was unveiled at CES 2022 but its TLens win was only confirmed 2024-04-08; Xvisio's SeerLens One (2022-07) never became a confirmed design-win; Sharp showed a polymer-tunable-lens camera module and a 175 g VR HMD at CES 2023 (poLight is 'in dialogue with SHARP', 2026-08-19); Meizu went from design-win PO (2023-01-24) to announcement (2023-03-30) to sale (June 2023); LLVision's Leion Pro went to mass production 1.2 months after being named (2023-04-04); and Varjo announced XR-4 (dual 20 MP passthrough, Focal Edition autofocus) on 2023-11-27, the day poLight declared its MR HMD design-win. First PO to launch has never exceeded ten months for a product that shipped.

segments.title: Enterprise XR and the Magic Leap 2 proof
segments.text: Lenovo ThinkReality A3 (2021-01-10), the US$21.88bn IVAS award (2021-03-26), Pico 4 (2022-10-18), PS VR2 (2023-02-22) and Magic Leap 2 (2022-09-30) defined the period; Yole's teardown 153 days after ML2's release (2023-03-02) found poLight's TLens in its 13 MP camera, still the only teardown-confirmed TLens in an XR headset.

segments.title: XR makers' TLens filings: poLight named twice
segments.text: Outside the Meta chain the sweep found TLens in filings from three XR makers and a tail of phone, industrial and lab applicants. Bosch's retinal-scanning data glasses (priority 2022-08-23, published 2024-02-29) say the varifocal lens 'could be configured as a TLens from poLight (Skoppum, Norway)', in the display path, not a camera. Lemon/ByteDance's gaze-driven XR camera autofocus (priority 2023-09-20, WO 2025-03-27, US published 2026-08-27, no office action) names 'a poLight lens' twice, once for thermal compensation: the only XR-maker camera text naming poLight, from Pico's parent. Zhuhai Mojie's AR-glasses filings (2025-12-30, published 2026-03-27 and 2026-05-01) list Tlens beside VCM and a zoom lens. OPPO (from 2022-10-21), Vivo, Hikrobot, Honor (beside liquid lenses), Yingda, a microscope maker and Zebra use the term generically. About one XR-maker filing a year since 2022; no Apple, Google, Snap or Xreal text uses it, and none ties a filing to a product.

segments.title: Platform exits and pivots
segments.text: Microsoft discontinued HoloLens 2 (2024-10-01) and handed IVAS to Anduril (2025-02-11), which teamed with Meta on EagleEye (2025-05-29) and won US$159m (2025-09-09); HTC sold part of its XR division to Google (Jan 2025); Magic Leap partnered with Google (2024-05-30, extended 2025-10-29) and Pegatron (2025-12-30) before pivoting to waveguide supply (2026-07-09); Quanta put US$20m into Vuzix. The enterprise headset market that bought TLens via Magic Leap has largely dissolved into component supply.

segments.title: China AI-glasses wave, fixed focus
segments.text: Baidu's Xiaodu glasses took 364 days from unveil (2024-11-12) to sale; HTC Vive Eagle (12 MP, <49 g) went from announcement to Taiwan availability in 18 days (2025-08-14 to 2025-09-01); Meizu StarV Snap (2025-10-30), Mentra Live (Dec 2025) and INMO Air 3 (2025) list 12-16 MP cameras with no autofocus stated; Huawei's AI Glasses (2026-04-20, 12 MP, 35.5 g) came 23 months after its audio-only Eyewear 2 and 12 days after the tease. Across this wave no shipping product discloses an autofocus actuator.

segments.title: Headsets and enterprise autofocus wins
segments.text: SnkeXR named TLens in its medical AR headset on 2025-10-31; Valve released Steam Frame (2026-09-18), 310 days after announcing it, with four monochrome tracking cameras; Pico teased Project Swan on 2026-03-02, named it Space Pro, cancelled its 2026-09-02 event and moved release to Q4 2026 (a leak says early October at US$2,899); Ant Group showed 'Look to Pay' demo glasses with a TLens camera (poLight CEO, 2026-08-06), an Alibaba-side trace beside Qwen N1 (previewed 2026-09-10, on sale 2026-10-13); Viture's Helix ships Q1 2027. Vuzix booked follow-on orders four times between 2026-03-31 and 2026-08-11. Q Tech's 2026-09-28 posting names '(e.g. Meta, Pico)' as example brand customers, and ByteDance's 2023 filing lists a poLight lens as one autofocus option; neither is a supply link. The CEO declined to locate Program B, so Pico Space Pro is one of several Q4-2026 candidates, with Alibaba's N1 the closest fit on timing.

headline_findings: Meta VR Glasses (announced at Connect on 2026-09-23, US$1,299.99, spring 2027) are the only announced consumer device due in 2026-2027 with documented autofocus passthrough ('passthrough with autofocus and depth' on Meta's developer pages); Varjo's enterprise XR-4 Focal Edition (announced 2023-11-27) already offers gaze-directed autofocus passthrough, and poLight declared an MR-headset design-win that day without naming the customer. A Reality Labs engineer's LinkedIn post, seen only as a forum screenshot of an auto-translation, is paraphrased as saying he led the autofocus work, which took years across the whole stack; Meta's gaze-driven autofocus passthrough patent (priority 2023-03-31) was granted 2026-02-10. None of these names an actuator or supplier.

Meta's own filings describe a window/polymer/glass-membrane/piezo tunable lens in TLens-like terms: the lens barrel with integrated tunable lens (priority 2022-07-26, granted 2026-05-19, continuation published 2026-09-17), the wide-FOV assembly (granted 2026-06-23), closed-loop capacitance sensing (priority 2023-08-28), a +/-50 V piezo driver IC (priority 2023-11-15) and an exposed-camera protective-sleeve design whose tunable lens may use a 0 to +/-5 D piezo membrane (priority 2025-02-12, published 2026-08-13). They fit an integrated bought part as well as an own membrane lens: Meta's side retrieved poLight's TLens Add-In pages on 2022-10-19, and a 2023 omnibus quotes TLens-class figures (~6 mW, ~2 ms, 10 cm to infinity) without naming poLight.

The five Meta texts read in full in round 3 (the driver IC; camera-module, exposed-camera and barrel-via applications published 2026-06-25, 2026-08-13 and 2026-09-17, the only tunable-lens camera items in an unverified listing of ~70 recent Meta publications; a thermal filing) never refer to TLens or poLight: the thermal 'Tlens' labels a temperature, and poLight appears only as cited prior art. The camera-module application (priority 2024-12-19; Chinese counterpart 2026-06-23) says existing modules glue on a 3x3 or 5x5 mm tunable lens, a size fitting TLens (3.2 mm element) or a liquid lens, and integrates one with wafer-level optics. With the pending moving-element MEMS autofocus, Meta covers three architectures and never says whether it buys or builds the tunable element.

Qingdao Goertek Vision, the XR arm of the assembler that builds Meta's and Pico's headsets, filed four head-mounted-device applications on 2024-06-03 and 2024-09-02 (published 2024-09-27, 2024-10-01 twice and 2026-03-10; all in substantive examination) whose dependent claims name a 'tunable lens TLens' or a 'T-Lens' zoom lens of piezo film over polymer. One sets VR video see-through focus from eye-tracking fixation and calls VCM focus of about 1 s unacceptable; the others cover sub-0.1 s multi-focus fusion, binocular-gaze focus for camera glasses and ROI focus. None names poLight or a customer, and Goertek's place on Phoenix rests on unattributed 2026-09-20 supply-chain reports plus Citi's 2026-09-24 note naming Goertek and Sunny key beneficiaries of the VR Glasses, so this is ODM familiarity with TLens-type autofocus, not a Meta supply link.

Other device makers drew the same stack without proving a purchase. Lemon/ByteDance's gaze-driven XR camera autofocus application (priority 2023-09-20, US published 2026-08-27) is the only XR-maker camera filing naming poLight: its options include 'a poLight lens incorporating piezoelectric actuators, deformable membranes' and a poLight lens for thermal compensation; Bosch's 2022 data-glasses filing names a poLight TLens only for a display-path varifocal lens. Samsung's smart-glasses filing (KR priority 2022-10-31, US published 2025-07-31) uses a 'tunable lens (T-lens)' of piezo film, glass membrane and polymer, without naming poLight, in a depth camera no announced Samsung product has (its November eyewear has one 12 MP camera, FCC 2026-10-01); Samsung also holds its own piezo-option tunable-lens grant (2025-12-02).

Chinese lens, module and ODM filings use 'Tlens' or 'T-lens' as a class term for voltage-driven membrane lenses, and five false positives were dropped from the sweep. Q Tech's 'T-lens device' (filed 2023-07-25, granted 2024-04-16), Jiangxi Shengtai's AF module (granted 2024-12-27) and Goertek's texts spell out poLight's piezo-film-on-polymer construction; Sunny's texts describe a liquid-filled element, from Sunny Opotech's T-lens-in-motor application (filed 2021-09-29, pending) to Zhejiang Sunny Optics' AR/VR front-camera lens with a 'Tlens module' (filed 2026-03-04, published 2026-05-12). Huaqin's VR see-through lens (granted 2025-04-08) mentions a 'T lens' once. Sunny Opotech's internal-focusing grant (2026-01-30) rejects TLENS for field curvature. Sunny is reported as the camera-module maker for Meta's AI glasses, and Citi (2026-09-24) names it a VR Glasses beneficiary without saying for which part; no source names the VR Glasses camera-module or actuator vendor.

Q Tech's 2026 filings concern TLens-type parts: an inline diopter QC method 'taking tunable lens TLens as an example' so every lens can be measured 'throughout mass production' (filed 2026-03-30, published 2026-06-09; claim 10 recites the stack) and a TOF module pairing a generically named 'Tlens' with metalenses (filed 2026-04-24, published 2026-09-04), both classed general camera. They sit between the CEO's 'under qualification', with capacity 'limited by only having one test machine' (2026-03-10), and 'tested and qualified' (2026-08-06). Two lines and a new final-test machine double capacity by end-2026, but the CEO says the Q Tech line is 'not really built for the capacity of that OEM' (2026-08-19) and programme units are 'likely coming from the Philippines'.

poLight's 2024-2026 publications and grants name no customer and are mostly manufacturing and reliability work: hexagonal dies for wafer packing (priority 2024-12-20), a lead-free lens (priority 2024-07-16; first lead-free lenses assembled by February 2026; 'some of the very biggest' OEMs want lead removed), a low-power hold-mode driver (Danish filing 2025-02-03, PCT 2026-08-06), thermal compensation from a 2021 priority (EP granted 2026-03-11) and ghost/flare mitigation (published 2026-03-05); the rest add a ring-actuated lens with a 3-30 mm membrane (priority 2024-10-29) and wobulation (published 2025-10-30, 2026-08-05). Only the driver's description uses the TLens name, so a customer's silence on the brand proves little, while Meta's own lens, barrel, control and driver filings keep an in-house membrane lens a live alternative.

Meta remains the leading candidate for the Q Tech-backed OEM, on one inference chain. Q Tech reported a vendor code from a 'major US customer' (2024-03-25), called it the 'US M brand' (2024-08-12) and on 2026-09-28 advertised an XR factory head serving brand customers '(e.g. Meta, Pico)'. DBS's 2026-08-26 Q Tech note (target cut to HKD 12.60) says on p.4 that a Meta project pairing Q Tech modules with poLight's lens is 'expected to enter mass production in 1H27' and that Q Tech's AR optical engines ship to Meta and Samsung. That is sell-side inference: DBS's 2026-05-08 Meta note omits poLight, Apple has been floated in DNB-attributed and forum posts, and Program C is a different top-tier US OEM.

Program A has two orders in three announcements: a ~NOK 1.7-1.8m qualification PO (2025-08-06, 50% firm, final half called 2026-02-11) and a NOK 0.7m follow-on (2026-06-18, deliveries 'likely second half of 2026'), about NOK 2.5m and still 'qualification' 14 months after the first order. poLight's first production-linked orders came 4.8 months before launch (Xiaomi watch), about 3 (Honeywell validation) and 10 (Magic Leap 2, attribution inferred); disclosed initial MP POs were NOK 0.36m (Magic Leap 2) and 2.9m (Meizu); failures surfaced 9-41 months after first orders. If Program A is the VR Glasses camera, a first production PO would fall in October 2026 to early 2027, probably small; a Q3 report still saying 'qualification' would weaken that reading.

Program B became poLight's first consumer AR|MR design-in on 2026-07-10: NOK 4.9m of POs since 2025-11-24, the three 2026 orders (NOK 4.0m) at mass-production price, 'release plan is this year' and Q4-2026 deliveries for 'a big company and a major player in the ecosystem'; the CEO declined to locate it. Alibaba's Qwen N1 fits the timing best: previewed 2026-09-10, two months after the design-in as at Meizu, on sale 2026-10-13, and affiliate Ant Group showed TLens 'Look to Pay' demo glasses. Pico Space Pro, Samsung/Google eyewear, Snap Specs and, weakly, Xreal Aura were unveiled earlier and fit only a Q4 sale. Only a teardown identifying poLight's PZT-MEMS lens, not just a membrane or 'T-Lens' part, settles it.

Meta's hiring around Connect is actuator-agnostic: a Camera and Depth Electrical Engineer for 'auto-focus electrical design' (posted about 2026-09-16 to 09-22), an Opto-Mechanical Engineer, Camera, for Active Alignment and mass-production ramp (2026-09-22), a next-generation smart-glasses sensor lead (about 2026-09-30) and an undated camera-system role live on 2026-10-06. Meta's careers site (via mirrors) and six job boards (2026-10-06) show no tunable-lens, piezo or TLens wording, and the only actuator-specific Meta posting, a closed Seoul role, gives VCM as an example. The closest Meta-TLens link is a forum-posted, undated excerpt of a former Meta DFx engineer ('DRI for TLens camera process development, drove 2 Eng mini-builds'), engineering-build language; a second excerpt's employer is cropped.

Negative or neutral signals: poLight has filed nothing since its 2026-09-21 TWedge order (checked to 2026-10-06), a weak negative because its same-day disclosure precedent, an unnamed MR-headset maker, shipped within weeks while the VR Glasses ship in spring 2027; the CEO, COO and CTO sold 1,109,586 shares at an average NOK 12.13 after an option exercise (reported 2026-08-27); no source reports autofocus on Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, Ray-Ban Display or Aria Gen 2; Meta's moving-element MEMS autofocus for passthrough is pending. No merchant competitor has announced an XR camera win. CML's last XR-facing article is dated 2025-05-12, though a 2026-04-30 PCT and an October-2026 job ad cite glasses and AR/VR, and its CTO reportedly left for Apple around March 2026; Optotune launched its 0.3 g EL-3.1-10.8 for 'high-volume OEM integration' on 2026-09-21 (20 mW against TLens's <6 mW); Varioptic stays industrial; Sheba had 17 staff in January 2026. The live alternatives are Meta's own membrane lens, its moving-element MEMS design or a VCM, which Q Tech's affiliate Actutek can supply. Decisive checkpoints: poLight's Q3 report (2026-10-29), CMD (2026-10-30) and Q4 report (2027-02-24) and VR Glasses teardowns (Apr-Sep 2027); 2027 patent actions show claim scope, not suppliers.
subtitle: Supplier signals from poLight, Q Tech, CML, Optotune and the module chain, dated against Meta, Apple, Samsung/Google, Snap, Xreal, Pico, Alibaba and other 2026-2027 launches; lead-time bands calibrated to poLight's 2019-2024 record, extended with Meta patents, job posts, Chinese supply-chain reports, module-maker sightings and a full-text patent sweep for 'TLens' and 'poLight' across all applicants.
foot: Sources: poLight/Q Tech filings, decks and transcripts, patent registers, Meta developer docs and job posts, Chinese supply-chain press, broker notes and forum-posted LinkedIn excerpts; 964 events and 133 windows, whose 69 round-3 patent items were checked twice on the registers (51 confirmed, 12 partly supported, 6 wrong; 5 false positives dropped). Patents name options, not supply contracts; poLight has never named Meta or said '2027'; the DBS 1H27 sentence is sell-side inference; 'T-Lens' is a generic Chinese term. Round 3: full-text patent sweep for TLens/poLight (2024-2026), every row checked on the registers by two independent checkers, synthesis audited by a 18-skeptic panel before publication.

estimate.reasoning: Round 2 closed at 0.62 (TLens in the VR Glasses at launch) and 0.80 (Meta is the Q Tech-backed OEM); round 3 lowers them to 0.58 and 0.78, because the patent sweep found no OEM text that ties TLens or poLight to a product and because two round-2 shortcuts are undone. Round 2's +0.02 rested on items that only show the VR Glasses have autofocus (the paraphrased engineer post, the gaze-driven AF grant of 2026-02-10, a calibration filing listing a PZT lens beside VCM, SMA and MEMS) and on Q Tech line status counted twice ('tested and qualified' on 2026-08-06; 'TLens + AR Mono Engine: Volume Delivery Achieved' on 2026-08-24, a bullet shared with optical engines), none of which discriminates the actuator. Decomposed, the first number is about 0.78 for Meta backing Program A, times about 0.8 that Program A is the VR Glasses camera rather than a later, higher-volume Meta glasses device (the OEM's need is 'much higher' than the Q Tech line, while Citi expects VR Glasses volume to be limited), times about 0.88 that qualification completes and TLens ships at launch, plus about 0.02 for routes outside Program A, which gives 0.57-0.58. Those terms are held down by dated counter-evidence: Program A was still 'qualification' on 2026-06-18 with no design-in, though the Phoenix display has been in mass production since May 2026 and poLight puts design-in after design lock and component qualification; programme units are to come from the Philippines; no Phoenix supplier list or Connect coverage names a camera-module or actuator vendor or links poLight; and alternatives are live (Meta's pending moving-element MEMS design, Optotune's high-volume liquid lens of 2026-09-21, Q Tech's affiliated Actutek VCM source, the CEO's read that AR/MR cameras mostly use VCM or no AF). The sweep's new rows net to about zero: Goertek's 2024 filings (one of four puts a TLens under gaze-driven VST focus; Goertek also builds for Pico, Sony and Xiaomi and is placed on Phoenix by unattributed supply-chain reports and by Citi's 2026-09-24 beneficiary note, neither naming a camera part) and Meta's +/-50 V piezo driver IC (priority 2023-11-15) add about +0.01, while Sunny's liquid-type 'Tlens module', Sunny Opotech's TLENS field-curvature critique and Meta's newer membrane texts that name no supplier take about -0.01; the camera-module application, now read as polymer or liquid, and the calibration filing were already round-2 evidence. Meta's piezo-membrane filings stay neutral on the supplier, since they fit a bought TLens-class part (its side retrieved poLight's TLens Add-In pages on 2022-10-19 and a 2023 omnibus quotes ~6 mW, ~2 ms, 10 cm to infinity) as well as an in-house membrane lens, and the first number stays above 0.5 mainly because the CEO described Program A as very advanced, high-end glasses for a big US OEM seven weeks before Meta announced a US$1,299.99 'VR Glasses' with autofocus passthrough. On identity, Q Tech's own documents (a 'major US customer' vendor code of 2024-03-25, called 'US M brand' on 2024-08-12; a 2026-09-28 posting naming Meta and Pico as example XR brand customers) and DBS's p.4 sentence keep Meta well ahead, but they form one chain: DBS's own Meta note (2026-05-08) omits poLight, Apple (camera glasses in mass production from Q2 2027 per Kuo) has been floated in a DNB-attributed article and forums, Google, Amazon and Snap run 2026-2027 camera-glasses programmes, and Programs A, B and C are different customers (CEO, 2026-08-19), so a second top-tier US OEM is in TLens camera design and Meta could be C rather than A. The sweep is neutral on identity: no US OEM's own text names TLens (Meta cites poLight only as prior art), Apple's tunable-lens filings are fluid-filled or SMA-driven prescription lenses and its one camera-side hit, a lens-measurement method, was dropped as off-topic, and Samsung and ByteDance hold pending US applications on the same stack, so 0.80 is trimmed to 0.78 rather than raised. The ByteDance filing naming 'a poLight lens' (priority 2023-09-20) moves neither number and does not single out Pico for Program B, because Samsung's 2022 smart-glasses T-lens filing is as specific and Alibaba's Qwen N1, previewed two months after the design-in and on sale 2026-10-13, with affiliate Ant Group's TLens demo glasses, fits the timing better. The dated tests are the Q3 report (2026-10-29) and CMD (2026-10-30), a Program A design-in or first production PO (if Program A is the VR Glasses camera, poLight's precedents put it in October 2026 to early 2027), the Q4 report (2027-02-24) and the first teardowns able to identify a poLight PZT-MEMS lens (Apr-Sep 2027).
